newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open just higher, await CPI.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open just higher, await CPI.

text.p: The Australian share market edged barely higher at the open on Wednesday as traders marked time ahead of the release of local fourth quarter inflation figures due at 0030 GMT.
The All Ordinaries index added 3.8 points to 2,408.0.
With conflicting economic data in the United States giving mixed signals to a volatility-ridden Wall Street, investors preferred to look locally, making a cautious start to the day.
"There is not much in it so far," said a Sydney broker.
"Most people are waiting to see the numbers before deciding which way to jump."
The modest gains were widely spread with most of the majors showing firmer prices.
"The leaders are all up a few. I thought the miners may have been weaker with commodities prices a bit softer, but they are holding up well."

The big banks also showed some form, attracting interest as players waited to assess the interest rate implications of the inflation figures. Westpac shares, up 1.9 percent at A$7.48 (US$5.76) and ANZ Bank scrip, up one percent at A$8.10 were the pick of the big four.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 43 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
